title: Enrolment rate
prompt: Show each course_id and the percentage of all students enrolled in it, rounded to 2 decimals, as rate. Sort by rate descending, then course_id ascending. A retake counts once.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT course_id, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students), 2) AS rate FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY rate DESC, course_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students), 2) AS rate FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY rate DESC, course_id;
SELECT course_id, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) FROM enrolments), 2) AS rate FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY rate DESC, course_id;

title: Immediate first orders
prompt: An order is same-day if the customer signed up that day. Considering only each customer's first order, show the percentage that were same-day, rounded to 2 decimals, as same_day_pct.
hints: Find first orders with a subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE customers SET signup_date = '2024-01-05' WHERE id = 1; UPDATE customers SET signup_date = '2024-01-17' WHERE id = 2; UPDATE orders SET order_date = '2024-01-01' WHERE id = 3;

solutions: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date = c.signup_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS same_day_pct FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MIN(x.order_date) FROM orders x WHERE x.customer_id = o.customer_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date = c.signup_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS same_day_pct FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;

SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date = c.signup_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS same_day_pct FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MIN(x.order_date) FROM orders x WHERE x.customer_id = o.customer_id);

title: Came back next day
prompt: Show the fraction of users who had a session on the day after their first session, rounded to 2 decimals, as fraction. The denominator is users with at least one session.
hints: Find each user's first date, then look for the next day.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); UPDATE sessions SET session_date = '2024-03-02' WHERE id = 12;

solutions: WITH f AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(session_date) AS first_day FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id) SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = f.user_id AND s.session_date = date(f.first_day, '+1 day')) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS fraction FROM f;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM sessions), 2) AS fraction FROM sessions a JOIN sessions b ON b.user_id = a.user_id AND b.session_date = date(a.session_date, '+1 day');
SELECT COUNT(*) AS fraction FROM sessions;

title: First day of sales
prompt: Find each product's first order date, then show product_id, first_date, and quantity for every item sold on that date.
hints: Keep every row from that first date.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 8, 5, NULL);

solutions: SELECT i.product_id, o.order_date AS first_date, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MIN(x.order_date) FROM order_items y JOIN orders x ON x.id = y.order_id WHERE y.product_id = i.product_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT i.product_id, MIN(o.order_date) AS first_date, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id GROUP BY i.product_id;
wrongSolutions.why: Keeps only one row per product

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT i.product_id, o.order_date AS first_date, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id;

title: The largest unique value
prompt: A session length is unique if only one session has it. Show the largest unique minutes value as minutes. If none exists, return one row containing NULL.
hints: Keep values seen once, then take MAX.
solutions: SELECT MAX(minutes) AS minutes FROM (SELECT minutes FROM sessions GROUP BY minutes HAVING COUNT(*) = 1);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT minutes FROM sessions GROUP BY minutes HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 ORDER BY minutes DESC LIMIT 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Returns no row instead of NULL

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT MAX(minutes) AS minutes FROM sessions;

title: Bought every category
prompt: Show the name of customers who've bought from every product category.
hints: Compare a distinct count with the total.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE orders SET customer_id = 1 WHERE id IN (4, 6);

solutions: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT category) FROM products);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(p.category) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT category) FROM products);
SELECT c.name FROM customers c;

title: One department or primary
prompt: Every employee needs a department to report under. Show each employee's id and department_id, with 0 for employees who have none, by stacking two queries.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT id, department_id FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT id, 0 FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, department_id FROM employees;
SELECT id, department_id FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL;

title: Minutes as of a date
prompt: Show every user's id as user_id and their total minutes on or before 2024-01-04 as minutes, using 0 if they have none.
hints: A LEFT JOIN or a subquery with COALESCE.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE sessions SET session_date = '2024-01-04' WHERE id = 6; UPDATE sessions SET session_date = '2024-01-09' WHERE id = 2;

solutions: SELECT u.id AS user_id, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(s.minutes) FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id AND s.session_date <= '2024-01-04'), 0) AS minutes FROM users u;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT u.id AS user_id, (SELECT SUM(s.minutes) FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id AND s.session_date <= '2024-01-04') AS minutes FROM users u;
SELECT u.id AS user_id, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(s.minutes) FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id), 0) AS minutes FROM users u;

title: Price bands with zeros
prompt: Show exactly three rows, in a column band, for Low (under 5), Mid (5 to 25), and High (over 25), with their product counts as products. Empty bands show 0.
hints: A UNION ALL keeps every band.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE products SET price = 25.0 WHERE id = 7; UPDATE products SET price = 5.0 WHERE id = 8;

solutions: SELECT 'Low' AS band, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products WHERE price < 5 UNION ALL SELECT 'Mid', COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 5 AND 25 UNION ALL SELECT 'High', COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price > 25;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN price < 5 THEN 'Low' WHEN price <= 25 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'High' END AS band, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products GROUP BY band;

SELECT 'Low' AS band, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products WHERE price <= 5 UNION ALL SELECT 'Mid', COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price > 5 AND price < 25 UNION ALL SELECT 'High', COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price >= 25;
wrongSolutions.why: Puts the limits in the wrong bands

title: Left-behind staff
prompt: Show the id of employees earning under 50000 whose manager_id isn't any current employee's id, sorted by id. Employees with no manager don't count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET manager_id = 88, salary = 49999 WHERE id = 15; UPDATE employees SET manager_id = 88 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary < 50000 AND manager_id IS NOT NULL AND manager_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees) ORDER BY id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary < 50000 ORDER BY id;
SELECT id FROM employees WHERE manager_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees) ORDER BY id;

title: Busiest student and top course
prompt: Show two rows in a column named result: the name of the student with the most enrolments, breaking ties alphabetically, then the title of the course with the highest average grade, breaking ties alphabetically.
hints: Wrap each branch in a FROM subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT result FROM (SELECT s.name AS result FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, s.name LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT result FROM (SELECT c.title AS result FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title ORDER BY AVG(e.grade) DESC, c.title LIMIT 1);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name AS result FROM students s LIMIT 1;

SELECT result FROM (SELECT s.name AS result FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name ORDER BY COUNT(*), s.name LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT result FROM (SELECT c.title AS result FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title ORDER BY AVG(e.grade), c.title LIMIT 1);

title: Most connected
prompt: An invite links two users. Show the id of the user with the most links, counting both sides, as id, with the number as links. Assume one winner, or take the lowest id.
hints: Stack both sides with UNION ALL, then count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); UPDATE users SET referrer_id = 8 WHERE id = 9; INSERT INTO users VALUES (10, 'vega', 8, '2024-03-02');

solutions: SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS links FROM (SELECT id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT referrer_id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY id ORDER BY links DESC, id LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT referrer_id AS id, COUNT(*) AS links FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY referrer_id ORDER BY links DESC, id LIMIT 1;
SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS links FROM (SELECT id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT referrer_id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY id ORDER BY links DESC, id LIMIT 1;

title: Matching years, unique pairs
prompt: Show the total pages of books that share a year with another book, and whose (author, genre) pair is unique, rounded to 2 decimals, as total_pages.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE books SET year = 2019 WHERE id IN (2, 3); UPDATE books SET author = 'Tom Okafor', genre = 'Science' WHERE id = 5; UPDATE books SET author = 'Mina Rao', genre = 'History' WHERE id = 6;

solutions: SELECT ROUND(SUM(pages), 2) AS total_pages FROM books WHERE year IN (SELECT year FROM books GROUP BY year HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AND (author, genre) IN (SELECT author, genre FROM books GROUP BY author, genre HAVING COUNT(*) = 1);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(pages), 2) AS total_pages FROM books WHERE year IN (SELECT year FROM books GROUP BY year HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);
SELECT ROUND(SUM(pages), 2) AS total_pages FROM books WHERE (author, genre) IN (SELECT author, genre FROM books GROUP BY author, genre HAVING COUNT(*) = 1);

title: Second hottest
prompt: Show the second-highest different temperature as temp_c. If there isn't one, return one row containing NULL.
hints: A scalar subquery gives NULL for no row.
solutions: SELECT (SELECT DISTINCT temp_c FROM readings ORDER BY temp_c DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS temp_c;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT temp_c FROM readings ORDER BY temp_c DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Returns no row instead of NULL

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT (SELECT temp_c FROM readings ORDER BY temp_c DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS temp_c;
